correctness.rationale: The proof exactly follows the anchor's definitions. For \(n<d\), the logical complement has \(d-n\ge1\) local edges. Since \(p_{\mathrm{net}}\ge p_{\mathrm{gate}}\), monotonicity gives \(-\log p_{\mathrm{net}}\le-\log p_{\mathrm{gate}}\), so the packet edge cannot exceed the complement cost. Strictness and the sole tie case are exhaustively characterized. The claim is expressly limited to the two-class comparison and therefore does not infer full MWPM correctness from this inequality.

value.rationale: The paper presents \(n_{\max}^{\mathrm{corr}}=\lceil d/2\rceil\) as a central design rule and motivates it by the local packet-versus-complement comparison. Showing that the same comparison actually favors every \(n<d\) changes the logical interpretation of that design rule: any genuine upper boundary below \(d\) must be justified by global matching alternatives or multi-fault effects. This is a substantive boundary correction, not a notation change or a routine recomputation.
